events.title: The founding of the Redemptorists
events.shortBlurb: St. Alphonsus Liguori gathered a handful of missioners at Scala to preach Christ to the most abandoned poor, choosing for the day the feast of the Lateran…
body: Alphonsus Maria de Liguori, a Neapolitan advocate turned priest, had been stirred by the plight of the herdsmen and country folk of the hills above the Amalfi coast, who lived almost without knowledge of the Gospel. Resting at Scala in 1730 near the sanctuary of Santa Maria dei Monti, he conceived a company wholly given to preaching missions among the most forsaken.

On 9 November 1732, in the humble oratory of a convent at Scala, with Bishop Tommaso Falcoia presiding at the Mass of the Holy Spirit, Alphonsus and a few companions founded the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer — the Redemptorists — under the motto "Copiosa apud eum redemptio," "with him is plentiful redemption." He was thirty-six, and the little band numbered fewer than ten. He chose the day deliberately, for it is the feast of the Dedication of the Lateran, the mother church of the world, a sign of the mission's universal reach.

Among the early members was St. Gerard Majella. Pope Benedict XIV gave the congregation formal approval on 25 February 1749. Alphonsus himself became a bishop and a moral theologian of the first rank, and was later named a Doctor of the Church.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “St. Alphonsus Maria de' Liguori”
